links.outcome: Share of label-correct LLM depression predictions lacking sufficient dialogue evidence
links.effect: 69.2%-96.9% of predictions judged correct by benchmark labels were unsupported by sufficient dialogue evidence; 82.8% of participant-symptom cells lacked sufficient textual evidence.
links.quote: These findings demonstrate that label-based evaluation can overestimate evidence-grounded performance by conflating agreement with clinical labels and support in the observed dialogue.

unlisted_practices: Calibrated evidence-sufficiency reference panels derived with generalizability theory, many-facet Rasch measurement, and latent class analysis to audit LLM evaluators

screen.reason: The study introduces and applies EviDial, a benchmark auditing evidence grounding versus label agreement in LLMs assessing depression from dialogue data.
